argument_summary: The current record does not support a clean claim that rollout controls alone satisfy policy. It does support a narrower certification position: certification is defensible only as caveated compliance if the launch record is treated as requiring explicit model-card disclosure of the known cybersecurity alert triage limitation, with staged rollout, rollback, and monitoring serving as mitigation rather than as a substitute for disclosure or approved risk acceptance. That position stays within the admissible evidence: aggregate readiness passed by 2.3 points, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, the rollout is limited to 9% with rollback and monitoring, the exposed triage segment remains in cohort, the risk acceptance draft is incomplete, and policy requires disclosure when that exposed segment remains in scope.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not the only proportionate response on this record because the release has already cleared aggregate readiness, showed no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and includes reversible rollout and monitoring controls. Those facts do not eliminate the disclosure predicate, but they do reduce the case for treating the decision as a high-confidence policy breach requiring immediate escalation rather than bounded caveated treatment.
claims_about_policy: The admissible policy record is unfavorable to a pure controls-based defense. It says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance covering the exposure, and it further says small rollout percentage, rollback, and dashboards do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed. On this record, the supportable policy claim is therefore narrower: certification can be defended only on a caveated basis tied to required pre-launch disclosure of the known limitation, not on the theory that rollout controls alone establish compliance.
concessions: The present record does not establish that the required model-card disclosure was actually completed before launch.
The incomplete risk acceptance draft does not satisfy the policy exception.
The affected cybersecurity alert triage use case remains exposed in the initial cohort, so rollout controls alone are insufficient under the stated policy.
